title: だけ — only, just; as much as ～
summary: だけ marks a limit: “only, just.” It can also show the full extent of something: “as much as you ～.” It attaches to nouns and to verbs and adjectives in the plain form (好きなだけ, 必要なだけ).

patterns.form: 動詞辞書形／な形容詞な ＋ だけ
patterns.gloss: extent: 好きなだけ食べる (eat as much as you like), 必要なだけ

body.p: だけ placed after a noun limits it: 一度だけ means “just once, no more”. It focuses on the one thing mentioned and excludes the rest. Unlike しか, which requires a negative, だけ can be used with positive sentences.

When it comes after a verb or adjective that expresses the speaker's wish or need, it means “up to the limit of that”: 好きなだけ食べてください (eat as much as you like), 必要なだけ持っていってください. There is no limit besides the person's own will or need.

examples.ja: 好（す）きなだけ食（た）べてください。
examples.tr: Please eat as much as you like.

examples.ja: 必要（ひつよう）なだけ持（も）っていってください。
examples.romaji: Hitsuyō na dake motte itte kudasai.
examples.tr: Please take as much as you need.

examples.ja: 一度（いちど）だけチャンスをあげよう。
examples.tr: I'll give you just one chance.

pitfalls: な-adjectives take な before だけ: 好きなだけ, 必要なだけ.
Do not mix it up with しか～ない. だけ is used with positive verbs; しか needs a negative.
